episodes.196328: During the very late evening and early morning hours of October 30th and 31st, a severe QLCS passed through the forecast area. This line produced wind gusts of up to 70 mph and produced sporadic wind damage. It also produced one tornado in Missouri during its passage.
episodes.196674: A series of cold fronts and a polar trough increased moisture and instability across the region for the last three days of October. Moisture levels went well above the climatological value, leading to a significant increase in showers and thunderstorms. Showers were very numerous, with rainfall accumulations surpassing 8 inches in sectors of northeastern and southeastern Puerto Rico. Soils were saturated, and rivers were running very high, triggering the issuance of a Flood Watch. With the excessive rainfall, multiple flash flooding events and mudslides unfolded.
episodes.197197: A series of cold fronts and a polar trough increased moisture and instability across the region to end October and start November. Above normal moisture, saturated soils, and rivers running high increased the risk of flooding. A Flash Flood Watch was in effect on November 1st with Debris Flow, Sinkholes, Flooding and Flash Flooding being reported in southeastern and north-central Puerto Rico.
episodes.198030: A broad upper level trough with embedded shortwave trough digs into the Pacific Northwest in early November. Bringing with it blustery winds and precipitation in various forms resulting in hazards and utility/infrastructure disruption.
episodes.198123: A near stationary strong thunderstorm caused flash flooding in parts of Webb Country, specifically over the eastern part of the City of Laredo.

events.narrative: Emergency Managers from Maunabo reported that PR-759 in Barrio Matuyas Bajo is flooded due to the Rio Maunabo overflowing its banks. The road is impassable.
Thunderstorm winds caused a 4 to 5 inch diameter tree to fall across Hwy Z. Steel truss metal and lumber was also reported across Hwy 151.
Thunderstorm winds blew shingles off of a house, knocked large tree limbs down, and damaged a new machine shed. The observed thunderstorm wind gust was measured with a Davis weather station.
OMME director reported landslides impacting a house and cars along PR-759 km. 3.9. Three adults and one infant were rescued with no injuries. Damages to the property and cars were reported.

Public shared a video in social media of a Sink Hole in a bridge (over Jacaboa river) along road PR-7755 in Bo. Jacaboa in Patillas due to heavy rain. Several Families are uncommunicated due to the situation. Approximately 2-3 inches have fallen combined with previous rainfall.
A landslide occurred in PR-198, near Francisco Torres School and the Emilio Huyke double-A baseball park in Las Piedras, affecting one lane of the roadway.
Honda Creek out of its banks flooded PR-31, KM14.9, leaving both lanes impassable. This is near Edgardo Auto Parts and the intersection with PR-936.
The 911 Call Center reported a car partly submerged in flood waters from rio Blanco, with one person trapped inside, near PR-31, KM 8.2, Dr. Jose Barbosa highway.
A completely flooded roadway was reported at PR-2, KM76 near a fast food restaurant, a beauty supply and a shopping center due to poor drainage. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Flooding was reported along road PR-2, KM 87.7 near Hatillo Town Center. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Emergency Managers reported that PR-2, KM 84.0 (Jose Joaquin Yiye Avila St.) in front of El Buen Cafe Restaurant was completely flooded with both lanes impassable.
Several days of rain led to rock slides, 3 miles north of Leytonville, CA.|Lat. 39.72N, Long. -123.50W.
Sheriff's office reported flooding along the frontage road of HWY-359 and mile marker 440 from efficient rainfall rates due to a strong near stationary storm.
